Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the streaming UX looked promising. A few quick clarifying items from our side so we can finalize the pilot matrix:

- Latency target: we want 95th percentile under 350ms for short-form responses (<=128 tokens). Is that achievable on hosted?
- Streaming behavior: we'd like response pre-token latency under 50ms and continuous streaming for partial tokens (websocket preferred).
- Concurrency: our initial plan is 800 parallel requests across 40 backend workers (roughly 20 RPS per worker). Will Redwood's connection pooling support stable KV cache reuse in that pattern?
- Backoff: if you hit rate-limits, we need graceful 429 semantics and a clear retry window so our client can fallback to cached answers.

Also, Samir asked to get a rough committed-concurrency quote for a 3-month pilot. Can you send a short matrix (pilot vs dedicated) we can use to score options?

Appreciate it — aim to lock pilot plan by EOD Friday.

Best,
Peter

Hi Peter — great to meet you and Samir today. High-level recap and concrete next steps below so we have a single source of truth for the pilot scoping:

Recap of requirements (from call):
- 95p latency target: 350ms for <=128 tokens (interactive prompts)
- Streaming: sub-50ms per-chunk latency, websocket streaming with chunked partial tokens
- Concurrency: target ~800 parallel requests at steady state; peak bursts up to 1,200 for short windows
- Desired behavior on throttling: 429 with Retry-After and a consistent backoff window; fallback to cached completions acceptable

Quick feasibility notes (see attached SLO sketch):
- Hosted API: we can meet 95p=350ms for short-form on our latest optimized model family for the pilot traffic profile assuming continuous batching and KV reuse. Bursty peaks will be absorbed via short-term burst capacity but may incur transient queuing.
- Streaming: websocket streaming supported; we've observed median chunk latency ~30–40ms in similar pilots.
- Concurrency & pooling: connection pooling with multiplexing is available; recommended approach is 40 persistent connections from your cluster to our endpoint with session affinity. That gives stable KV cache hit rates and reduces cold-kernel invocations.

Requested deliverables from Redwood (next steps):
1) Pilot concurrency matrix (hosted vs dedicated) with committed concurrency levels and price bands — Ben will draft this today.
2) Technical notes on connection pooling + Retry-After semantics — Aditya adding details below.
3) Short pilot acceptance criteria doc for your QA — I can draft by tomorrow if you want.

I attached a quick sketch (slo-sketch-connpool.png) that shows expected tail behavior and when we'd recommend dedicated capacity. Ben, Aditya — can you please stitch together the pilot quote + connection guidance?

Peter/Samir — can we schedule a 30 min tech sync Fri 10:00am PT to finalize numbers? If that works I'll send the invite.

Thanks,
Grace

Hi Peter — quick tech note to be explicit on pooling and SLO guards so your infra team can evaluate:

- Recommended client topology: 40 long-lived TCP/TLS connections from your aggregator layer to our endpoint. Each connection should support multiplexing (HTTP/2 or websocket multiplex) so you can open many logical streams without policing OS ephemeral ports.
- KV cache reuse: persistence of per-session KV caches requires session affinity. With 40 connections we expect >70% KV hit for a 800-parallel workload when request hotspots are stable. If your traffic has high fanout across many small tenants, hit rates drop — call this out and we can model.
- Backpressure and 429s: Redwood returns 429 with Retry-After. For streaming sessions we return a structured JSON error with retry_window_ms and a recommended jittered-backoff formula. For pilots we recommend exponential backoff starting at 200ms, cap at 10s, and failover to cached result on third retry.
- Burst handling: hosted plan provides limited short-term burst credit; for predictable sustained peaks (>1 minute at 1200 concurrent) we recommend Dedicated capacity.

I'll attach a simple calculation for pilot sizing: assuming avg. response cost ~1.8 tokens/ms and median token count 60, the 95p budget maps to X GPU slots — Ben will translate to SKUs and price bands.

If helpful, I can run a short synthetic against your shape next week to validate numbers.

Cheers,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Peter / Samir — thanks for the fast turnaround this week. Attached is the pilot quote spreadsheet (finova-pilot-matrix.xlsx) with two clear paths:

1) Hosted Pilot (30 days, burst-capable):
   - Committed concurrency band: 400 | 800 | 1200 (discount tiers)
   - Rate-limits: per-connection qps of 50, account-level ingress throttle at 10k rps soft ceiling for hosted pilots; hard caps applied per plan
   - Expected 95p latency (<=128 tokens): 350ms achievable at 800 committed concurrency with recommended 40-connection pooling and streaming enabled

2) Dedicated Pilot (reserved capacity on dedicated GPU pool):
   - Committed concurrency guaranteed: 800 with configurable burst to 1,500 for short windows
   - No account-level soft-throttle; per-endpoint SLOs and SLAs available

Operational notes:
- If you choose Hosted and hit sustained >1 minute peaks above 1,000 concurrent, we'll propose a brief migration plan to Dedicated or a tiered overflow policy.
- Pricing assumptions and sample monthly cost per band are in tab B of the attached.

Next steps I recommend:
- Confirm the Fri 10am PT tech sync and we'll present the spreadsheet live (we can walk numbers and sizing).
- If you want, we can run a 2-hour synthetic with your token distribution on Mon to validate 95p. Aditya can run that with your test key.

Happy to adjust the matrix if you have a preferred committed concurrency number.

Best,
Ben Carter
